parent.description: The parent resource of the log view. This specifies the project and location where the log view is located and determines the scope of the IAM policy.
parent.rationale: Proper parent configuration ensures IAM policies are applied to the correct log view resource and inherit appropriate organizational context and security boundaries.

location.description: The geographic location of the log view. If not specified, it will be parsed from the parent resource identifier or taken from the provider configuration.
location.rationale: Location specification ensures IAM policies are applied to the correct regional instance of the log view, which may impact data residency and compliance requirements.

bucket.description: The name of the logging bucket that contains the log view. This identifies the specific bucket resource for IAM policy application.
bucket.rationale: Correct bucket identification ensures IAM policies are applied to the intended log storage resource and prevents accidental access to unrelated buckets.

name.description: The name of the log view to which the IAM policy applies. This specifies the exact log view resource within the bucket.
name.rationale: Precise log view identification ensures IAM policies target the correct log data view and prevent unintended access to other views within the same bucket.

member/members.description: The identity or identities that will be granted the privilege specified in the role. Each entry can be a specific user, service account, group, domain, or special identifier.
member/members.rationale: Proper member specification is critical for implementing the principle of least privilege and ensuring only authorized identities can access sensitive log data.

role.description: The role that should be applied to the specified members. This can be a predefined role or a custom role following the proper format.
role.rationale: Role assignment must follow the principle of least privilege, granting only the minimum permissions necessary for the intended function.

policy_data.description: The IAM policy data source that defines the complete policy to be applied to the log view. This allows for complex policy configurations from a data source.
policy_data.rationale: Policy data must be carefully constructed to ensure proper access controls and avoid unintended privilege escalation or access grants.

condition.description: Optional conditions that specify when the IAM binding is in effect. This allows for time-based or attribute-based access control.
condition.rationale: Conditions enable fine-grained access control but must be properly configured to avoid security gaps or unintended access restrictions.

expression.description: A CEL (Common Expression Language) expression that defines the condition under which the IAM binding is active.
expression.rationale: The expression must be carefully crafted to enforce intended access controls without creating security vulnerabilities or unintended access patterns.

title.description: A short name for the condition, used to identify it in audit logs and error messages.
title.rationale: While the title itself doesn't impact security, clear naming helps with auditability and management of conditional access policies.

description.description: A detailed description explaining the purpose and scope of the condition. This helps with audit trails and policy management.
description.rationale: Clear documentation of condition purposes ensures proper auditability and helps security teams understand the intent behind conditional access rules.
